# Data dictionary

> **Demonstration data. Synthetic records, not ARDE/KUBAHO data.**

*Generated by `src/model.py` on 15 October 2026 from the warehouse (`data/warehouse/arde.duckdb`) and `config/data_dictionary.yaml`. Do not edit by hand: change the YAML file instead.*

The warehouse is a star schema: **fact** tables hold events and results; **dimension** tables describe them (what, where, when, who). Every fact row has `source_file`, `source_sheet` and `source_row`, so any number can be traced to the Excel row it came from. Rows that broke a critical data-quality rule are in `quarantine`, not in the facts. The same tables are exported to `data/exports/` as CSV and Parquet for Power BI.

No table holds names, phone numbers or national ID numbers. People and donors are identified by salted hashes (`beneficiary_key`, `donor_key`).

## Tables

| Table | Kind | Rows | Key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dim_programme` | dimension | 2 | programme_id | One row per programme. |
| `dim_project` | dimension | 5 | project_id | One row per project. Each project belongs to one programme. |
| `dim_activity` | dimension | 15 | activity_id | One row per type of activity a project runs (the activity list, not each event). |
| `dim_location` | dimension | 152 | location_id | One row per village, plus one row per district (for results reported at district level, such as monthly indicator reports). District rows have no sector, cell or village. Provinces and districts are Rwanda's real ones; sectors, cells and villages are synthetic while on demonstration data. |
| `dim_indicator` | dimension | 13 | indicator_id | One row per MEAL indicator in config/indicator_catalogue.yaml (draft, for co-design with ARDE/KUBAHO staff). |
| `dim_date` | dimension | 1,461 | date | One row per calendar day, with Rwanda's fiscal year (July to June). |
| `dim_beneficiary` | dimension | 1,509 | beneficiary_key | One row per person (after duplicate matching). No names, phone numbers or ID numbers: the person is identified only by a salted hash. Details come from the person's earliest registration that passed the data-quality checks. |
| `dim_donor` | dimension | 25 | donor_key | One row per donor. Organisations keep their names; individual donors appear only as "Individual donor #NNN". Contact names, emails and phone numbers are never stored. |
| `fact_activity` | fact | 2,728 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | One row per activity event from the activity monitoring files and digitised paper records. Rows that broke a critical rule are not here: they are in the quarantine table. |
| `fact_beneficiary_service` | fact | 4,475 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | One row per service a registered person received. |
| `fact_indicator_result` | fact | 581 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | One row per indicator value reported in the monthly indicator reports (per project, district, month and, where relevant, sex). Rows that broke a critical rule are in the quarantine table instead. |
| `fact_opportunity` | fact | 30 | opportunity_id | One row per funding opportunity in the donor tracker. |
| `dq_results` | data quality | 14 | rule_id | One row per data-quality rule (config/dq_rules.yaml), with how many records it checked and how many broke it. |
| `dq_rule_results_by_file` | data quality | 183 | source_file, source_sheet, rule_id | Every data-quality rule scored separately for each source file and sheet, for finding which rule drives a low score. |
| `dq_dimension_scores` | data quality | 7 | dimension | One row per data-quality dimension, plus an "overall" row (the average of the six). |
| `dq_by_source_file` | data quality | 26 | source_file, source_sheet | One row per Excel file and sheet read, with how many of its rows had problems. |
| `dq_by_field_officer` | data quality | 4 | field_officer | One row per field officer (activity records, indicator reports and registers that carry an officer code), with their data-quality results. |
| `quarantine` | data quality | 235 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | Every row that broke a critical rule, with the reasons. These rows are kept here, not in the fact tables, until the source Excel file is corrected and the pipeline is run again. |
| `review_queue` | data quality | 282 | source_file, source_sheet, source_row | Every row with warnings (and no critical problem). The row is used in results, but a person should check it. |
| `skipped_sheets` | data quality | 0 | source_file, source_sheet | Every sheet the pipeline could not read, with the reason and the column headers it did not recognise. |
| `dq_info_measures` | data quality | 6 | metric_id | Data-quality measures shown on the dashboard instead of rows to review (info-level flags). |
| `report_completeness` | data quality | 417 | project_id, district, period | One row per monthly indicator report that was due, and whether it arrived. |
| `indicator_values` | indicator | 6,853 | value_id | One row per indicator value: for each indicator, source (reported or derived), project, district, period and breakdown. "All" in project_id or district means all projects or all districts together (worked out directly, not by adding up the rows below, so a person is never counted twice). |
| `indicator_value_sources` | indicator | 99,567 | value_id, source_table, source_file, source_sheet, source_row, record_key | Traceability: for each indicator value, every record it was worked out from. Use it to go from any number on the dashboard back to the Excel rows. |
| `indicator_reconciliation` | indicator | 916 | indicator_code, project_id, district, period_type, period, disaggregation | A key MEAL check: where an indicator is both reported and derived LIKE FOR LIKE (catalogue: derived.like_for_like), the two values side by side, for every month (by project, district and breakdown) and, for indicators compared by quarter, every quarter. The catalogue's derived.reconcile sets the COMPARISON LEVEL (month or quarter, totals only): only rows at that level can be flagged. Gaps above the tolerance (settings: indicators.reconciliation_tolerance_pct) AND at least the minimum difference (reconciliation_min_difference) are flagged. A month with a report but no matching records counts as derived 0. A quarter adds up only the months that have a report, on both sides. Other rows (breakdowns by sex, months of a quarterly indicator) are for information. |

## `dim_location`

One row per village, plus one row per district (for results reported at district level, such as monthly indicator reports). District rows have no sector, cell or village. Provinces and districts are Rwanda's real ones; sectors, cells and villages are synthetic while on demonstration data.

Rows: 152. Key: location_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `location_id` | VARCHAR | Location code. LOC0001-style codes are villages; DIST-<district> codes are whole districts. |
| `province` | VARCHAR | Province (Kigali City, Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western). |
| `district` | VARCHAR | District (one of the 30). |
| `sector` | VARCHAR | Sector (empty for a district row). |
| `cell` | VARCHAR | Cell (empty for a district row). |
| `village` | VARCHAR | Village (empty for a district row). |
| `location_level` | VARCHAR | village or district. Each fact table links to one level only (fact_activity to villages, fact_indicator_result to districts), so never add up rows of different levels; group by the district column instead. |

Rows: 13. Key: indicator_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|

| `higher_is_better` | BOOLEAN | True if a higher value is good (the direction of the indicator). |

| `owner` | VARCHAR | Who is responsible for the indicator (to be confirmed with partner). |

## `dim_beneficiary`

One row per person (after duplicate matching). No names, phone numbers or ID numbers: the person is identified only by a salted hash. Details come from the person's earliest registration that passed the data-quality checks.

Rows: 1,509. Key: beneficiary_key.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `beneficiary_key` | VARCHAR | Pseudonymous person key (salted hash). The same for every registration of one person. |
| `sex` | VARCHAR | female or male (empty if never recorded clearly). |
| `age_band` | VARCHAR | Age at registration, in bands (e.g. 25-34). |
| `household_size` | BIGINT | Number of people in the household. |
| `disability_flag` | BOOLEAN | True if the person reported a disability. |
| `location_id` | VARCHAR | Village where the person registered (links to dim_location); the district only, when the village was not recorded. Empty when all of the person's registrations are quarantined. |
| `pending_duplicate_review` | BOOLEAN | True if any of this person's records is waiting for a duplicate review. A people count includes these, so it may be slightly too high until the review is done ("includes N people pending duplicate review"). |

## `fact_activity`

One row per activity event from the activity monitoring files and digitised paper records. Rows that broke a critical rule are not here: they are in the quarantine table.

Rows: 2,728. Key: source_file, source_sheet, source_row.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `activity_id` | VARCHAR | Which activity (links to dim_activity). |
| `location_id` | VARCHAR | Village where it took place (links to dim_location). |
| `date` | DATE | Day it took place (empty if cancelled or not yet done; links to dim_date). |
| `participants_total` | BIGINT | Number of participants. |
| `participants_female` | BIGINT | Number of women and girls. |
| `participants_male` | BIGINT | Number of men and boys. |
| `cost_rwf` | DOUBLE | Cost in Rwandan francs. |
| `planned_date` | DATE | Day it was planned for. |
| `entry_date` | DATE | Day it was typed into Excel. |
| `status` | VARCHAR | planned, completed, delayed or cancelled. |
| `on_time` | BOOLEAN | True if completed within the allowed days of its planned date (on_time_tolerance_days in settings), False if delayed, cancelled or completed late, empty if it cannot be checked (planned, or only the month is known). |
| `officer_code` | VARCHAR | Code of the field officer who ran the activity, where the source file gives it. |
| `quality_flag` | VARCHAR | ok, or the worst problem left on this kept row: info (only counted) or warning (in the review queue). Rows with a critical problem are in the quarantine table, not here. |
| `source_file` | VARCHAR | Excel file the row came from. |
| `source_sheet` | VARCHAR | Sheet in that file. |
| `source_row` | BIGINT | Row number in that sheet, as shown in Excel. |

## `dq_results`

One row per data-quality rule (config/dq_rules.yaml), with how many records it checked and how many broke it.

Rows: 14. Key: rule_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | VARCHAR | Rule code, e.g. COM-02. |
| `dimension` | VARCHAR | completeness, validity, consistency, uniqueness, timeliness or accuracy. |
| `description` | VARCHAR | The rule in plain English. |
| `records_checked` | BIGINT | Number of records (or sheets, or expected reports) the rule applies to. |
| `records_failed` | BIGINT | Number that broke the rule. |
| `score` | DOUBLE | Percentage that passed (0 to 100). |
| `critical_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that quarantined a row. |
| `warning_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that sent a row to the review queue. |
| `info_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that are only counted. |
| `dimension_impact` | DOUBLE | Points this rule takes off its dimension score (the dimension score is the average of its rules), to show which rule is driving a low score. |

| `dimension` | VARCHAR | The rule's dimension. |

| `records_failed` | BIGINT | Records in this sheet that broke it. |
| `score` | DOUBLE | Percentage that passed (0 to 100). |
| `critical_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that quarantined a row. |
| `warning_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that sent a row to the review queue. |
| `info_failures` | BIGINT | Failures that are only counted. |

## `indicator_values`

One row per indicator value: for each indicator, source (reported or derived), project, district, period and breakdown. "All" in project_id or district means all projects or all districts together (worked out directly, not by adding up the rows below, so a person is never counted twice).

Rows: 6,853. Key: value_id.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value_id` | BIGINT | Number of the value (links to indicator_value_sources). |
| `indicator_id` | BIGINT | Indicator (links to dim_indicator). |
| `indicator_code` | VARCHAR | Indicator code, e.g. AGR-01. |
| `source` | VARCHAR | reported (from the monthly indicator reports) or derived (worked out from activity and beneficiary records). |
| `aggregation` | VARCHAR | How months roll up into quarters and years (catalogue): sum (they add up), latest (the latest month's snapshot), average, or ratio (worked out again from the records for the whole period). |
| `project_id` | VARCHAR | Project, or All. |
| `district` | VARCHAR | District, or All. |
| `period_type` | VARCHAR | month, quarter (fiscal quarter, Q1 = July to September) or fiscal_year. |
| `period` | VARCHAR | Period label, e.g. 2024-03, FY2023/24 Q3, FY2023/24. |
| `period_start` | DATE | First day of the period. |
| `disaggregation` | VARCHAR | total, or sex=female / sex=male. |
| `unit` | VARCHAR | number, percent, hectares or RWF. |
| `target` | DOUBLE | Target for the period (empty when no target is set, or when some months have no target). |
| `actual` | DOUBLE | Value for the period (empty when no data arrived). |
| `pct_achieved` | DOUBLE | Actual as a % of target (empty when there is no complete target). |
| `status` | VARCHAR | on track, at risk, off track, no target set, target incomplete (some months have no target: no traffic-light colour), or no data. |
| `partial_pct_achieved` | DOUBLE | When the target is incomplete: actual as a % of target over the months that DO have a target (see target_note). |
| `partial_target` | DOUBLE | When the target is incomplete: the target added up (or averaged) over the months that DO have a target. |
| `partial_actual` | DOUBLE | The actual over the same months as partial_target (so the two can be compared fairly). |
| `target_note` | VARCHAR | For an incomplete target, e.g. "partial: 9 of 12 months". |
| `months_with_target` | BIGINT | Months in the period that have a value and a complete target. |
| `months_with_data` | BIGINT | Months in the period that have a value (for a "latest" indicator, 1 - the month used). |
| `numerator` | DOUBLE | The numerator behind the value (e.g. women reached), where the indicator is a ratio. |
| `denominator` | DOUBLE | The denominator behind the value (e.g. people reached with sex recorded). |
| `coverage_pct` | DOUBLE | How much of the relevant data the value could be worked out from, e.g. the % of planned activities whose timing could be checked, or the % of expected reports received. |
| `n_rows` | DOUBLE | Number of source records used. |

## `indicator_value_sources`

Traceability: for each indicator value, every record it was worked out from. Use it to go from any number on the dashboard back to the Excel rows.

Rows: 99,567. Key: value_id, source_table, source_file, source_sheet, source_row, record_key.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value_id` | BIGINT | The indicator value (links to indicator_values). |
| `source_table` | VARCHAR | The warehouse table the record is in (fact_activity, fact_beneficiary_service, fact_indicator_result or report_completeness). |
| `source_file` | VARCHAR | Excel file the record came from. |
| `source_sheet` | VARCHAR | Sheet in that file. |
| `source_row` | BIGINT | Row number in that sheet, as shown in Excel. |
| `record_key` | VARCHAR | For report_completeness, which report (project|district|month); otherwise empty. |

## `indicator_reconciliation`

A key MEAL check: where an indicator is both reported and derived LIKE FOR LIKE (catalogue: derived.like_for_like), the two values side by side, for every month (by project, district and breakdown) and, for indicators compared by quarter, every quarter. The catalogue's derived.reconcile sets the COMPARISON LEVEL (month or quarter, totals only): only rows at that level can be flagged. Gaps above the tolerance (settings: indicators.reconciliation_tolerance_pct) AND at least the minimum difference (reconciliation_min_difference) are flagged. A month with a report but no matching records counts as derived 0. A quarter adds up only the months that have a report, on both sides. Other rows (breakdowns by sex, months of a quarterly indicator) are for information.

Rows: 916. Key: indicator_code, project_id, district, period_type, period, disaggregation.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `indicator_code` | VARCHAR | Indicator code. |
| `indicator_id` | BIGINT | Indicator (links to dim_indicator). |
| `project_id` | VARCHAR | Project. |
| `district` | VARCHAR | District. |
| `period_type` | VARCHAR | month or quarter. |
| `period` | VARCHAR | Month (e.g. 2024-03) or fiscal quarter (e.g. FY2024/25 Q3). |
| `period_start` | DATE | First day of the month or quarter. |
| `disaggregation` | VARCHAR | total, or sex=female / sex=male. |
| `comparison_level` | BOOLEAN | True if this row is at the level where gaps are flagged (catalogue derived.reconcile). |
| `months_compared` | BIGINT | Months in the row that have a report. |
| `reported` | DOUBLE | Value from the monthly indicator reports (added up over the months compared). |
| `derived` | DOUBLE | Value worked out from the activity and beneficiary records (over the same months). |
| `difference` | DOUBLE | Derived minus reported. |
| `pct_difference` | DOUBLE | Difference as a % of the reported value. |
| `tolerance_pct` | BIGINT | The tolerance used. |
| `status` | VARCHAR | within tolerance, gap above tolerance, or derived only (records but no report). |
| `flag` | BOOLEAN | True if the row is at the comparison level and the gap is above the % tolerance and at least the minimum difference. |
| `reported_value_id` | BIGINT | The monthly reported value (links to indicator_values); empty for quarter rows. |
| `derived_value_id` | BIGINT | The monthly derived value (links to indicator_values); empty for quarter rows. |
